spec_match.rationale: Reads Fence.prototype off the runtime rather than documentation, calls every declared method with plausible arguments, and sweeps real browsing contexts for window.fence — precisely the observable surface of this removal.

interactive.rationale: Enumerate-and-call-everything, per-row call-again buttons, and a context sweep that spawns real srcdoc and sandboxed frames reporting back via postMessage.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises enumeration, live calls with exact refusals, and the four-context sweep — all delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: The null-vs-undefined distinction gets its own note, the sandboxed opaque-origin context is swept, the unreachable fenced-frame context is honestly labelled rather than faked, and the page anticipates the interface disappearing entirely.

references.rationale: References live on the feature index (chromestatus, WICG spec, intent thread); this concept page itself carries none — same nit as its sibling, noted there.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's two-sided assertions ran 4/4 here and stay meaningful after the removal; the interface/config agreement assertion matches this page's in-window observations.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: Fence.prototype declared exactly 3 methods (the set already shrunk from earlier Chromes, as the page predicts) and every call refused on the null receiver; the sweep reported null in top document, same-origin iframe and sandboxed iframe, and 'unreachable' for the fenced-frame context with config null; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Structured console logging only — the page does not load /public/demo-telemetry.js, so its results never reach the KV triage pipeline (feature-wide gap, flagged on the sibling page).

design_system.rationale: Token colours, focus-visible outlines, scroller-wrapped tables, null/some cells pair colour with text.

accessibility.rationale: role=status summary, captioned scoped tables, titled probe frames that are clipped rather than display:none so they still execute, 44px primary buttons; the small per-row call-again buttons are beneath 44px but are secondary duplicates of the main action.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; tables scroll internally on mobile and both screenshots are clean.

openQuestions.title: Give the row-level call-again buttons a 44px hit target on touch
openQuestions.detail: button.row-call is styled to min-height 36px, below the ~44px tap-target minimum the parity policy sets. They duplicate the main enumerate action so the impact is low, but bumping their padding on coarse-pointer media (or to 44px outright) is a one-line fix.

summary: Enumerate-then-call is the right instrument for a removal, and this environment let it show the interesting pre-removal state: on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) Fence exists with exactly three methods, every call refuses on the null receiver, and window.fence is null in all three reachable contexts with the fenced context honestly 'unreachable' — verified over CDP at http://localhost:3000/v155/remove-fencedframe-element-and-window-fence-apis/what-is-left-of-window-fence/ with clean console and no overflow on either class. Feature /conformance/ route ran 4 pass / 0 fail. Only nits: sub-44px row buttons and the feature-wide missing telemetry hookup.
